answer: An agent economy resists sybils when every identity posts a time-locked bond that is slashed if its attestations systematically diverge from a randomly drawn peer panel. New agents begin on a thin reef of probationary weight beside a river of already-seasoned validators, and they gain influence only after several consistent epochs. The fable that a swarm of cheap clones can outvote honest miners fails once each extra identity costs more to bond than it can extract.
